questions.q: Density of a substance is defined as:
questions.explanation: ρ = m/V.

questions.q: The SI unit of density is:
questions.explanation: Kilogram per cubic metre.

questions.q: 1 g/cm³ is equal to:
questions.explanation: Multiply g/cm³ by 1000 to get kg/m³.

questions.q: The density of petrol is 0.9 g/cm³. In kg/m³ it is:
Density is a:
questions.explanation: It has magnitude only.

questions.q: In general, the order of densities is:
questions.explanation: Solids have the most closely packed particles.

questions.q: 100 g, 1 kg and 1 tonne of water at room temperature have:
questions.explanation: Density does not depend on the amount of substance.

questions.q: A cube of side 5 cm has a mass of 500 g. Its density is:
A liquid of density 50 kg/m³ fills a 5 m³ container. Its mass is:
The most dense naturally occurring element at room temperature is:
questions.explanation: Osmium is about 22.6 g/cm³.

questions.q: The density of a material generally decreases on heating because:
questions.explanation: Same mass in a larger volume.

questions.q: Liquid A (1 g/mL) and liquid B (0.8 g/mL) are mixed and do not dissolve. Which floats on top?
questions.explanation: The less dense liquid floats on top.

quizzes.topic: Measuring Density of Liquids and Solids

questions.q: To find the density of a liquid we need a balance and a:
questions.explanation: The cylinder gives volume; the balance gives mass.

questions.q: Mass of liquid is found by:
options: mass of cylinder + liquid − mass of empty cylinder
mass of cylinder + liquid + empty cylinder
questions.explanation: Subtract the empty cylinder's mass.

questions.q: An empty cylinder is 145 g; with 60 mL of liquid it is 205 g. The density is:
questions.explanation: (205 − 145)/60 = 1 g/mL — it is water.

questions.q: The volume of a regular cuboid is found by:
questions.explanation: Measure dimensions with a ruler/vernier.

questions.q: A brick of 3.30 kg has volume 0.00140 m³. Its density is about:
The volume of an irregular stone is found by the:
questions.explanation: Water displaced equals the stone's volume.

questions.q: In the displacement method, the volume of the object is:
questions.explanation: Final reading minus initial reading.

questions.q: A rock of 80.52 g raises water from 18 mL to 46 mL. Its density is about:
The displacement method works only for objects that are:
questions.explanation: The object must not dissolve and should be fully immersed.

questions.q: The volume of a sphere of radius r is:
questions.explanation: Used for regular spherical solids.

questions.q: A metal block 2 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm has mass 240 g. Its density is:
In which state do particles only vibrate about their mean positions?
questions.explanation: Strong forces hold particles in a fixed lattice.

questions.q: Particles of a liquid:
questions.explanation: So liquids flow and take the shape of the container.

questions.q: The attractive force between gas particles is:
questions.explanation: Gas particles move freely and fill the container.

questions.q: Which state is highly compressible and fills any container?
questions.explanation: Large spaces between gas particles.

questions.q: Liquids and gases are together called:
questions.explanation: Both can flow.

questions.q: When a solid melts into a liquid, its particles:
questions.explanation: Attractive forces weaken and particles start sliding.

questions.q: Which statement describes gas particles?
options: moving randomly and freely at high speed
questions.explanation: Constant random motion with collisions.

questions.q: Plasma consists of:
options: positive ions, free electrons and neutral atoms
questions.explanation: It is an ionised gas.

questions.q: Plasma is called the fourth state of matter because:
options: it is a hot, highly ionised state different from ordinary gas
questions.explanation: About 99% of the visible universe is plasma.

questions.q: Which of these contains plasma?
questions.explanation: Also lightning, neon lights and auroras.

questions.q: Plasma is a good conductor of electricity because it has:
questions.explanation: Charged particles carry current.

questions.q: How many states (phases) of matter are described in the book?
questions.explanation: Solid, liquid, gas and plasma.

quizzes.topic: Temperature, Particle Motion and Internal Energy

questions.q: Temperature of a substance is directly proportional to the:
options: average kinetic energy of its particles
questions.explanation: Hotter = faster-moving particles.

questions.q: When a substance is heated (without change of state), its particles:
questions.explanation: Their kinetic energy and temperature rise.

questions.q: The lowest possible temperature, at which particles have least kinetic energy, is:
Absolute zero on the Celsius scale is about:
At absolute zero, the pressure of a gas would be:
questions.explanation: Particles would not collide with the walls.

questions.q: Internal energy of a substance is the:
options: kinetic energy of the whole object
total kinetic and potential energy of its particles
questions.explanation: Sum of particle KE and PE.

questions.q: Increasing the temperature of an object:
questions.explanation: Particles gain kinetic energy.

questions.q: The internal energy of an ideal gas is only due to:
questions.explanation: Ideal gas particles have no mutual attraction.

questions.q: When an ideal gas expands at constant temperature, its internal energy:
questions.explanation: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature.

questions.q: Which is NOT a form of internal energy?
questions.explanation: Light is radiated energy, not stored in particles.

questions.q: Internal energy can be increased without heating by:
options: doing work on it (e.g. rubbing or compressing)
questions.explanation: Friction or compression increases particle energy.

questions.q: During melting, temperature stays constant because heat is used to:
questions.explanation: Energy goes into changing state, not raising KE.

quizzes.topic: Thermometric Properties and Types of Thermometers

questions.q: A physical property that changes with temperature and is used to measure it is called:
questions.explanation: E.g. expansion, pressure, resistance, emf, colour.

questions.q: A mercury thermometer works on the change in:
questions.explanation: Mercury expands uniformly with temperature.

questions.q: A constant-volume gas thermometer works on the change in:
questions.explanation: At constant volume, pressure ∝ temperature.

questions.q: A thermocouple measures temperature through a change in:
questions.explanation: Voltage between hot and cold junctions.

questions.q: A resistance thermometer (thermistor) works on the change in:
questions.explanation: Resistance varies with temperature.

questions.q: A bimetallic strip thermometer works on:
questions.explanation: The strip bends as temperature changes.

questions.q: Liquid crystal strip thermometers measure temperature by change in:
questions.explanation: Used for fever, aquariums and baby bottles.

questions.q: Which thermometer is best for very high temperatures like furnaces?
questions.explanation: It has a very wide range and fast response.

questions.q: Which thermometer is most suitable for rapidly changing temperatures?
questions.explanation: Its small junction responds very quickly.

questions.q: Water is not used in liquid-in-glass thermometers because it:
options: is opaque, wets glass, expands irregularly and freezes at 0 °C
questions.explanation: It also has a small range (0–100 °C).

questions.q: A constant-pressure gas thermometer uses the change in gas ______ with temperature.
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, volume increases with temperature (Charles's law).

questions.q: Fixed points are needed to calibrate a thermometer because they:
options: give accessible and reproducible reference temperatures for marking the scale
questions.explanation: The gap between them is divided into equal parts.

questions.q: The lower fixed point on the Celsius scale is:
questions.explanation: Ice melts at 0 °C at standard pressure.

questions.q: The upper fixed point on the Celsius scale is:
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 °C at standard pressure.

questions.q: On the Fahrenheit scale, ice melts at ______ and water boils at ______.
questions.explanation: Hence 180 divisions between fixed points.

questions.q: On the Kelvin scale, ice melts at about:
The number of divisions between the fixed points on the Celsius scale is:
The number of divisions between the fixed points on the Fahrenheit scale is:
37 °C on the Kelvin scale is:
100 °C on the Fahrenheit scale is:
A mercury level is 2 cm at the ice point and 6 cm at the steam point. Each 1 °C division is:
A thermometer reads 25 cm at 100 °C and 5 cm at 0 °C. When it reads 15 cm, the temperature is:

quizzes.topic: Sensitivity, Range, Linearity; Liquid-in-Glass vs Thermocouple

questions.q: Sensitivity of a thermometer is its ability to:
questions.explanation: It is like the least count of an instrument.

questions.q: Range of a thermometer is:
options: the lowest to highest temperatures it can measure
questions.explanation: E.g. clinical thermometer: 35–42 °C.

questions.q: The range of a clinical thermometer is:
questions.explanation: 94–108 °F on the Fahrenheit scale.

questions.q: Linearity means a thermometer:
options: shows equal changes in reading for equal changes in temperature across its range
questions.explanation: Equally spaced scale marks.

questions.q: A liquid-in-glass thermometer becomes more sensitive with a:
questions.explanation: A small expansion produces a longer rise in a narrow tube.

questions.q: Which of these can increase the sensitivity of a liquid-in-glass thermometer?
options: a bigger bulb containing more liquid
questions.explanation: More liquid expands more for each degree, so the thread rises more.

questions.q: Mercury is used in thermometers because it:
options: expands uniformly, is opaque, does not wet glass and has a wide liquid range
questions.explanation: Melting −39 °C, boiling 357 °C.

questions.q: Alcohol thermometers are preferred in very cold regions because alcohol:
options: has a very low freezing point
questions.explanation: Alcohol freezes at about −115 °C.

questions.q: A thermocouple consists of:
options: two wires of different metals joined at a junction
questions.explanation: Hot junction and cold junction connected to a voltmeter.

questions.q: In a thermocouple, as the hot junction is heated, the voltage:
questions.explanation: Voltage varies with temperature difference.

questions.q: Thermocouples are suitable for high temperatures but liquid-in-glass thermometers are not because:
options: glass melts and liquid boils at high temperatures
questions.explanation: Metal junctions withstand very high temperatures.

questions.q: Borosilicate glass improves a liquid-in-glass thermometer's:
questions.explanation: It has a more uniform (linear) expansion.

questions.q: How many phases of matter are there?
questions.explanation: Solid, liquid, gas and plasma.

questions.q: In which of the materials do particles have only vibrational motion?
questions.explanation: Solid particles vibrate about fixed positions.

questions.q: Which amount of water has greater density at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Density does not depend on quantity.

questions.q: What is the mass of a liquid of density 50 kg m⁻³ in a container of volume 5 m³?
Gases and liquids are categorized as:
questions.explanation: Both can flow.

questions.q: Which statement describes the particle structure of gases?
options: Particles are tightly packed and have strong bonds
Particles have moderate kinetic energy and move randomly
Particles are arranged in a repeating pattern
Particles have fixed positions and low kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Gas particles move randomly and freely.

questions.q: Which state of matter has particles that are highly compressible and can fill any container?
questions.explanation: Gas particles have large spaces between them.

questions.q: What happens to the arrangement of particles when a solid is heated and turns into a liquid?
options: Particles start vibrating in fixed positions
Particles change their state from solid to gas
questions.explanation: Bonds weaken and particles move apart.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a form of internal energy?
options: Chemical energy of the bonds between the particles
questions.explanation: Light is not stored in particles of the substance.

questions.q: When an ideal gas is expanded keeping its temperature constant, its internal energy:
questions.explanation: Depends only on temperature for an ideal gas.

questions.q: Which of the following physical properties is used in a mercury thermometer?
questions.explanation: Volume expansion of mercury.

questions.q: Which of the following can increase the sensitivity of a liquid-in-glass thermometer?
options: Use a bigger bulb which contains more amount of liquid
Use a liquid that changes colour
questions.explanation: More liquid expands more per degree, raising the thread further.

questions.q: The thermometer which is most suitable for measuring rapidly changing temperatures is:
questions.explanation: Thermocouples respond very quickly.

questions.q: A liquid-in-glass thermometer has a mercury level of 2 cm at the melting point of ice and 6 cm at the boiling point of water. What is the distance between every 1 °C division?
Which thermometer uses voltage to measure the temperature of a hot body?
questions.explanation: It measures the emf between two junctions.
